Ryuichi Sakamoto — Opus (2023)

Knowing that his time was drawing to an end, Ryuichi Sakamoto, legendary Japanese composer who gave many films their musical soul, sat down at his piano for one last performance.
No audience. No spectacle. Just a man, his piano, and a lifetime of devotion. A deeply intimate testament to the beauty and fragility of being human, and to the extraordinary power of art to touch the soul.
words inspired by Mahmoud Darwish (a bed for the stranger 1998)

a famous quote by the 13th-century Persian poet and Sufi mystic Rumi.

Recognition, not discovery:  it suggest that love can be a deep and sudden recognition of a soul connection that already exists before two people physically meet.

Union as a reunion: In Sufi mysticism, it is believed that lovers share the same divine essence. Meeting someone you love in the physical world is just a reflection of an eternal bond your souls share beyond time. 

Wholeness: You're not looking for another person to complete you. Instead, you approach a relationship from a place of inner wholeness, seeing your partner as a mirror for your own spiritual growth.

One of the most compelling aspects of A Bronx Tale is the relationship between Calogero, known
as "C." and Sonnv. What begins as a young boy's
fascination with the neiahborhood mob boss
gradually develops into a complex father-son
dynamic that shapes Calogero's understanding of
life, loyalty, and respect.

Sonnv is evervthing Calogero's hardworking father
fears: powerful, feared, and connected to a
dangerous world. Yet Sonnv also becomes a
mentor, teaching Calogero lessons that go far
bevond crime and street life. Some of the film's
most memorable moments come from Sonnv's
wisdom, including his famous belief that beinc
respected is often more valuable than being loved.

What makes their relationship so interesting is that
Sonnv genuinelv cares about Calogero and wants
him to avoid the mistakes that trapped him in the
jife he chose. At the same time, Calogero finds
himself torn between two father figures: the
honest, hardworking values of Lorenzo and the
charisma, influence, and street wisdom of Sonny
Rather than portraying Sonny as simply a villain or
a hero, A Bronx Tale presents him as a deeplv
human character filled with contradictions. 

His bond with Calogero becomes the emotional heart
of the film, turning what could have been a
standard gangster story into a thoughtful
coming-of-age tale about choosing the kind of man
you want to become.

a return to a love—or wholeness—that was once natural, but became lost in confusion and time before the heart could express it's truth. Not a plea for reunion, but the rediscovery of what remained beneath the separation: a love transformed into courage, devotion and a shelter within.

Perhaps the sacredness of love lies not in whether a bond endures or finds its way back to life, but in refusing to abandon the truth it awakened within us—and allowing that light to continue to guide us.

A still from Bernardo Bertolucci’s The Dreamers (2003). An exploration of youth, desire, rebellion, cinema, and the refusal to accept the world as it is by following the seductive refuge of fantasy—and the moment reality comes crashing through the window, demanding that we grow up. 

What happens when we leave that dream? Do we lose all meaning?—or is it where eventually an even deeper magic and freedom can be found once we fully enter life?
